instructions: Add a new string slice field to the server configuration struct, e.g., `ClientCertSanSuffixAllowList []string`.
In the configuration loader, read the `AEGIS_PROXY_CLIENT_CERT_SAN_SUFFIX` environment variable. If set, split its value by comma and populate the allow-list field.
Document the new configuration option in code comments and any relevant configuration documentation.
edits.rationale: Adding a configuration field for the SAN suffix allow-list enables administrators to define and document remote access restrictions, supporting AC-17a.[01]-[03]. Wiring this to an environment variable ensures configuration/connection requirements are established and manageable.

instructions: During TLS handshake or session initiation, extract the SANs from the presented client certificate.
If the allow-list is non-empty, check that at least one SAN in the client certificate ends with an allowed suffix. Reject the connection if not.
On session start, log the subject and serial number of the client certificate using the existing logging framework, ensuring the log entry is associated with the session.start event.
Ensure logs are structured and include enough context for audit and investigation.
edits.rationale: Enforcing a SAN suffix allow-list on client certificates ensures only authorized remote clients can connect, directly supporting AC-17b. Logging the subject and serial of client certificates on session start provides an auditable record of remote access, supporting AC-17a.[01] and AC-17a.[03].

instructions: Add a new environment variable entry for `AEGIS_PROXY_CLIENT_CERT_SAN_SUFFIX` in the proxy container spec.
Document the purpose of this variable in deployment notes or comments.
Ensure the variable is optional (can be unset or empty for no restriction).
edits.rationale: Wiring the `AEGIS_PROXY_CLIENT_CERT_SAN_SUFFIX` environment variable into the deployment manifest ensures the allow-list policy is managed as part of the deployment configuration, supporting documented and authorized remote access per AC-17.

plan.summary: To strengthen compliance with NIST AC-17 and FedRAMP High for remote access controls, the proxy service will introduce a client certificate SAN suffix allow-list policy, log client certificate details on session start, and wire the allow-list policy to deployment configuration. These changes further restrict and document remote access, provide enhanced auditability, and ensure configuration is managed and authorized per AC-17 requirements.
